title: fix: preserve coordinator errors and recover cached results
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Preserves original coordinator/cache errors and reset, overload, and retryable flags in the existing Tinybird error stack; no schema change or new public error details.
- Checks the existing cache once after a coordinator RPC failure. Returns the saved result if present, otherwise 503; never restarts a job or makes another AI request.
- Reuses normal cache-hit billing: recovery and a later identical request produce one provider call, one wallet debit, and one billed event. Recovered requests are not logged as failed requests in Tinybird.
- Verified 141 focused tests, Gen typecheck, and Biome. No deployment or secret changes.

gist.headline: The cache catches the falling acorn
gist.blurb: When a coordinator stumbles, the hive now checks whether the answer already made it safely into the cache. Same result, no extra AI trip, no duplicate pollen toll.
gist.summary: Generation deduplication now preserves coordinator error flags and, after a coordinator RPC failure, checks the existing cache once to return any saved result without restarting the job or issuing another AI request.
gist.impact: Requests that recover from a coordinator hiccup can receive their already-generated result through the normal cache-hit path, with one provider call, one wallet debit, and one billed event.
gist.visual_concept: Depict generation recovery as a cozy garden delivery: Polli notices a small coordinator terminal briefly sputter, then finds a finished glowing response safely stored in a cache jar. A CRT monitor robot can eagerly hold the recovered result while a single path from the AI garden to the cache emphasizes that no second provider journey or duplicate billing occurs.
